source.version: Journal version of record (open access): Proceedings of the Design Society, Volume 6: DESIGN 2026, pp. 507-516, https://doi.org/10.1017/pds.2026.10409
source.title_on_document: Evaluating TRIZ with and without LLM support: an experimental study on engineering problem-solving

supplement.holds: No supplement or online appendix is mentioned. Data and materials are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request (p. 515, Data availability).

paper_design_summary: Engineering students each solved one of three engineering design problems (polymer gear testing rig GT, mounting bracket MB, wind turbine power maximization WT) individually and were randomly assigned to use the TRIZ contradiction matrix with an LLM assistant (TRIZ-C+LLM, Copilot Smart GPT-5 recommended, with a prompt pack) or the TRIZ contradiction matrix alone (TRIZ-C, triz40.com, no LLM). Expert raters with PhDs in mechanical engineering scored each student's top-ranked solution on feasibility, requirements, innovativeness, and elaboration (1-7), averaged into design quality; students also completed a post-task survey on workload, usefulness, and satisfaction.

studies.label: Main experiment: TRIZ-C+LLM vs TRIZ-C on three engineering problems (GT, MB, WT)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Method: TRIZ contradiction matrix with LLM-based AI assistant (TRIZ-C+LLM) or TRIZ contradiction matrix only (TRIZ-C). The problem was not randomized: each problem was given to a distinct student group at a distinct location (GT and MB part of a course).
assignment.quote: Each student solved one problem only and was randomly assigned the method to use, either TRIZ-C+LLM or TRIZ-C.

arms.name: TRIZ-C+LLM
arms.description: TRIZ contradiction matrix supported by an LLM-based AI assistant; prompt pack for problem framing, contradiction identification, inventive principle suggestions, solution generation, diversity check; Microsoft Copilot Smart GPT-5 recommended, other LLM assistants allowed if reported. Analyzed N: GT 10, MB 10, WT 43, total 63.

arms.name: TRIZ-C
arms.description: TRIZ contradiction matrix only, with access to https://www.triz40.com/; asked not to use LLM-based AI assistants. Analyzed N: GT 11, MB 10, WT 30, total 51.

participants.exclusions: One GT student did not understand the engineering problem and was excluded (Table 1 note; GT curriculum count is 22 but N1 = 21, so about 115 students performed the assignment, though the paper gives no count at assignment). Design quality analyzed for 114 (Table 2). One MB student (TRIZ-C+LLM) did not answer the survey, so survey outcomes use 113 (62 TRIZ-C+LLM, 51 TRIZ-C). A pilot study (Group 1, Location 1) on GT and WT is described without a sample size and is not analyzed.
participants.who: Engineering students: GT mainly fourth-year mechanical engineering (22); MB Erasmus exchange master students, mostly mechanical engineering background (20); WT fourth- and fifth-year industrial engineering students specialized in AI (73).
participants.country: not_stated (three unnamed locations; author affiliations in Slovenia, Sweden, Morocco, Canada)
participants.quote: N1: number of students performing the assignment ... *One student did not understand the engineering problem and was therefore excluded from the study.
participants.locator: p. 510 (PDF p. 4), Table 1 and note; p. 512 (PDF p. 6), Table 2

ai_tool.name_model: Microsoft Copilot with Smart GPT-5 recommended; students free to choose other LLM-based AI assistants but had to report which one
ai_tool.how_used: Students prompted the LLM, guided by a prompt pack, to search for contradictions, suggest TRIZ inventive principles, and generate specific solutions, then developed the most promising solution. Participants got a 30-min TRIZ presentation and a 15-min prompt engineering presentation plus a practice problem beforehand.

task.description: Engineering conceptual design problems: develop a concept for alternating loading of polymer gears in a test rig (GT), a bracket mounting an electrical drive on a bicycle frame (MB), or a concept to maximize wind turbine power (WT). Students selected contradictions, generated ideas from at least three inventive principles, and developed and documented their top-ranked idea.
task.duration: Planned about 45 minutes (students could use more or less time); mean completion TRIZ-C+LLM 40.3 min (SD 20.9), TRIZ-C 46.2 min (SD 21.3).

outcomes.name: Design quality (expert-rated, mean of four criteria)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Average of four criteria rated 1-7 by experts holding PhDs in mechanical engineering: C1 feasibility, C2 requirements, C3 innovativeness, C4 elaboration. GT and MB: two experts with domain experience, scores averaged per criterion; WT: one other independent expert. Criteria are not reported separately. Analysis: two-way ANOVA Problem x Method with simple effects.

contrasts.reported: Total: TRIZ-C 4.8 (SD 0.90, N 51) vs TRIZ-C+LLM 5.6 (SD 1.13, N 63); main effect of Method F(1, 108) = 3.21, p = .076, 'which is not significant'; Problem x Method interaction F(2, 108) = 7.58, p = .001; Levene F(5, 108) = 2.88, p = .018.
GT: TRIZ-C 4.9 (SD 0.91, N 11) vs TRIZ-C+LLM 4.6 (SD 1.17, N 10); simple effect F(1, 108) = .51, p = .479.
MB: TRIZ-C 4.2 (SD 0.98, N 10) vs TRIZ-C+LLM 4.2 (SD 0.93, N 10); simple effect F(1, 108) = .06, p = .809.
WT: TRIZ-C 5.0 (SD 0.78, N 30) vs TRIZ-C+LLM 6.2 (SD 0.62, N 43); simple effect F(1, 108) = 34.67, p < .001.

outcomes.name: Student satisfaction with the final result (self-assessed quality of own solution)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Post-experimental online survey item on satisfaction with results, seven-point scale; shown in parentheses in Table 2. Correlates with expert design quality rho(113) = 0.38, p < .001. Not scored on the output by raters, so it does not meet criterion 3.

contrasts.reported: Total: TRIZ-C 4.3 (SD 1.44, N 51) vs TRIZ-C+LLM 4.7 (SD 1.22, N 62); independent samples t-test, satisfaction with results p = .119. By problem (Table 2): GT 4.4 (1.75) vs 3.7 (1.25); MB 3.7 (1.25) vs 4.0 (0.87, N 9); WT 4.5 (1.36) vs 5.1 (1.07).
contrasts.locator: p. 512 (PDF p. 6), Table 2; p. 513 (PDF p. 7), Section 4.3

company_involvement.description: No company involvement stated. Funding from Slovenian Research and Innovation Agency, GREENTECH (NextGenerationEU), GenAID Erasmus+, and Lise Meitner professorship fund (Lund University).

data_and_code.data_url: Available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request (p. 515)

eligibility.reason: Students were randomly assigned individually to TRIZ with an LLM assistant or TRIZ alone (p. 510); 114 students analyzed for design quality (Table 2, p. 512); design quality is expert-rated on each student's solution and includes an innovativeness criterion. Randomization was within problem groups at three locations; GT (21) and MB (20) subgroups are each under 50, WT alone has 73. The outcome is a composite design quality score (feasibility, requirements, innovativeness, elaboration), not a pure creativity rating.

one_line_finding: Expert-rated design quality was 5.6 with TRIZ+LLM vs 4.8 with TRIZ alone overall (Method F(1,108) = 3.21, p = .076), driven by the WT problem (6.2 vs 5.0, F = 34.67, p < .001), with no difference on GT (4.6 vs 4.9) or MB (4.2 vs 4.2) (p. 512, Section 4.2, Table 2).
open_questions: Construct coding of design quality: a composite of feasibility, requirements, innovativeness, and elaboration. Coded here as usefulness (codebook lists 'quality' there); overall_creativity or other are defensible. Innovativeness (C3) alone is not reported.

Whether the three problem groups (GT, MB, WT at different locations with different populations) should be separate studies or sample_ids; the paper analyzes them jointly in one two-way ANOVA, and only WT (73) passes the 50-person rule alone.

Count at assignment: Table 1 lists 22 GT students by curriculum but N1 = 21 after one exclusion, implying about 115 started; the paper does not state when the excluded student was assigned or to which arm.
Arm sizes are unbalanced in WT (43 vs 30); the paper does not describe the randomization procedure.
notes: Single 10-page proceedings paper with no supplement. Other survey outcomes are self-reported and not scored on the output: workload (difficulty defining contradictions TRIZ-C+LLM M = 3.18, SD 1.52 vs TRIZ-C M = 4.37, SD 1.55, t(111) = -4.123, p < .001, d = -0.779; overall problem difficulty 3.31 vs 4.27, t(111) = -3.784, d = -0.715), perceived usefulness (p = .133), idea quality with TRIZ (p = .099), innovation gain (p = .321), feasibility perception (p = .945), enjoyment (p = .271), use TRIZ again (p = .541); Figure 4 shows means with SE bars only (p. 513). Mental effort was asked only of MB and WT students. Pilot study with Microsoft Copilot GPT-5 on GT and WT (Group 1) has no reported sample or results.
